summary:
"Space Mission Adventure" is an educational game for children aged 7 to 12. It is based on real NASA data and allows players to build and launch rockets on missions to the Moon, Mars and Europa, a moon of Jupiter that is covered in ice. The game includes things like managing a budget, a store for spacecraft and equipment, planning trajectories, a rating system, an "Open Space" mode that is like a sandbox, and a "Spacecraft Lab."

The project solves this problem by changing complex engineering problems into easy-to-use solutions. While flying, players must avoid asteroids and collect coins to spend on new spacecraft and parts. They work with a limited budget and buy essential equipment like power systems and communication antennas. If there is not enough or the wrong kind of equipment, the rocket will not be able to launch. Players have to deal with things like mass, power and communications while working out how long it will take to get to faraway planets. After that, the game gives them a report on how well they did

This is important because students rarely get the chance to design a mission from start to finish. By doing experiments, the game teaches you how rocket launches work, how to plan missions, and how to deal with engineering trade-offs. It helps children to think in a logical way and solve problems, encouraging them to be the next generation of space explorers and to think like real NASA engineers.
details:
Project Summary & Vision

Space Mission Adventure is an interactive, cross-platform educational platform designed to make spacecraft engineering, orbital mechanics, and planetary exploration accessible and engaging for students and young learners. By transforming complex aerospace engineering challenges into an intuitive gameplay experience, the project bridges raw scientific data with interactive learning.

How It Works & NASA Data Integration

Powered by authentic blueprints, historical telemetry, and scientific datasets from real NASA missions, the game allows users to design, equip, and launch spacecraft toward the Moon, Mars, and Europa. Players must manage limited budgets, calculate trajectories, and balance critical parameters such as mass, power systems, and communication equipment—experiencing firsthand the real trade-offs faced by aerospace engineers.

Technology & Development

Built to run seamlessly across computers, tablets, and mobile phones, the platform utilizes modern web technologies. To efficiently implement complex game mechanics and logic, our team utilized Claude AI as a development assistant, while all core conceptualization, game design, and creative architecture were entirely developed by our team.

Impact & Future Explorers

Space Mission Adventure fills a unique gap by giving students the rare opportunity to design a space mission from start to finish. By fostering logical thinking, problem-solving, and a deep appreciation for space science, the project aims to inspire the next generation of space explorers and scientists.
